classified_object.notes: ISSF-governed rifle, pistol, and shotgun competition is used as a low-locomotion embodied sport reference; no single discipline is generalized beyond common structural features.

institutional_recognition.notes: ISSF publishes current international rulebooks and championship formats.

performance_agency.summary: Athlete precision, timing, posture, and trigger execution materially determine the shot during the firing sequence.
performance_agency.performance_window: From authorized preparation through shot release and scored series completion.

performance_interface.summary: The body acts through a regulated firearm and shooting position; mediation is conventional equipment rather than a computational arena.

embodied_performance.summary: Embodiment is fine-motor, balance, respiratory, and sensorimotor rather than locomotor.

arena.summary: A physical range, firing line, target distance, and safety zones structure performance.

rules.summary: ISSF rules define equipment, positions, timing, scoring, protests, and finals formats.

tracking.summary: Electronic targets and result systems may sense impacts and timing, but computational tracking is not the athlete’s arena.

measurement.summary: Shot value and series totals are precisely measured under declared target and timing rules.

comparability.summary: Comparability is engineered through event classes, equipment control, target specifications, timing, and officiating.

officiation.summary: Officials and electronic scoring systems jointly administer results and protests.

outcome_openness.summary: Scores emerge from athlete execution under constraints.

consequence_structure.summary: Ranking, qualification, elimination, and medal outcomes follow from contest structure.

operational_spatial_integration_profile.summary: Computational systems may support measurement and officiation, but the performance arena remains physical and the spatial-athletic core is not established.

classified_object.notes: Pocket billiards under WPA rules is used as a fine-motor physical-geometry case; the analysis does not generalize to every cue-sport discipline.

institutional_recognition.notes: WPA describes itself as the international governing body for pocket billiards and publishes world rules.

performance_agency.summary: Players exercise live aiming, stroke, speed, spin, and positional judgment during each inning.

performance_interface.summary: Direct bodily action is mediated by cue, balls, cloth, rails, and table geometry.

embodied_performance.summary: Embodiment is predominantly fine-motor and sensorimotor with modest locomotor and physiological demand.

arena.summary: A physical table with pockets, rails, spots, and ball positions is rule-bearing space.

rules.summary: WPA rules define legal strokes, fouls, turns, racks, and winning conditions.

tracking.summary: Standard play does not require computational tracking; human observation is primary.

measurement.summary: Ball state, legally pocketed balls, racks, and match scores are observable and recorded.

comparability.summary: Table and equipment specifications plus common rules support comparison, subject to venue conditions.

officiation.summary: Referees apply fouls and resolve disputes in governed events.

outcome_openness.summary: The table state and match result emerge through player execution.

consequence_structure.summary: Rack, match, ranking, and elimination effects derive from contest structure.

operational_spatial_integration_profile.summary: The activity demands sophisticated physical spatial reasoning, but no computationally mediated space is operationally integrated by default.

objections: The word spatial naturally describes positional skill, creating semantic confusion.

what_would_change_judgment: A contest where computational geometry jointly changes legal positions, measurement, or officiation as a constitutive arena.

provisional_finding.summary: Cue sports confirm that spatial skill and rule-bearing physical geometry are not Operational Spatial Integration. “Spatial” in everyday skill language must not be confused with the Altis category term.

limitations: This record focuses on WPA pool, not snooker, carom, or every local equipment condition.

classified_object.notes: The object is the regulated rehabilitation product and supervised exercise configuration, not stroke rehabilitation as a whole and not a competitive sport.

institutional_recognition.notes: FDA-cleared interactive rehabilitation exercise device; clinical support system rather than sport governance.

outcome_openness.summary: Therapeutic task completion is not an open competitive outcome.

consequence_structure.summary: Functional progress, adherence, fatigue, and clinical risk are meaningful consequences, but not contest consequences.

operational_spatial_integration_profile.summary: The system is strongly embodied and computationally mediated, but its correct class is Spatial Support System because therapeutic purpose and protocol replace contest structure.

classified_object.notes: The object is the physical Systems Competition in which human teams design and supervise autonomous robot teams searching a physical course.

institutional_recognition.notes: DARPA technology challenge with published final-event rules and prize structure.

performance_agency.summary: Human design and supervisory decisions matter, but robots perform substantial autonomous navigation and search during the timed run.
performance_agency.performance_window: Across pre-run system design and configuration, command-post supervision, and autonomous course execution.

performance_interface.summary: Humans interact through command systems while autonomous robots act physically in the course.

embodied_performance.summary: The decisive physical execution is robotic rather than live human bodily performance.

arena.summary: Physical subterranean courses and computational maps jointly structure robot operation and scoring.

rules.summary: DARPA rules define team composition, course constraints, reports, time, and scoring.

tracking.summary: Robots use perception, localization, networking, and mapping to detect artifacts and report locations.

measurement.summary: Correct artifact type and location within tolerance produce points; time resolves ranking.

comparability.summary: Common courses, report limits, location tolerance, and time frame support comparison, while system architectures vary by design.

officiation.summary: DARPA systems and officials validate artifact reports and scores.

outcome_openness.summary: Results emerge through team design, supervision, and autonomous system execution.

consequence_structure.summary: Points, time, ranking, and prize awards form the consequence structure.

operational_spatial_integration_profile.summary: The competition has rich operational spatial integration, but not human athletic embodiment. It is an engineering contest outside the Spatial Athletic core.

classified_object.notes: The object is a historical Formula E race under the FANBOOST rule, not current Formula E and not fan voting in sport generally.

institutional_recognition.notes: FIA Formula E championship mechanism used through Season 8 and discontinued from Season 9.

performance_agency.summary: Drivers retain live vehicle-control agency; fan votes allocate an optional power resource but do not execute the driving action.
performance_agency.performance_window: During the race, including the driver’s decision whether and when to deploy the awarded boost.

performance_interface.summary: Driver performance is mediated by a regulated racing vehicle and controls.

embodied_performance.summary: Vehicle control, endurance, sensorimotor coordination, cognitive demand, and physiological load remain decisive.

arena.summary: The racing arena is a physical street circuit. Fan voting occurs outside the arena.

rules.summary: The competition rule allocated extra power to selected drivers and constrained deployment.

tracking.summary: Vehicle telemetry and race timing measure the physical contest; fan votes determine eligibility for the boost.

measurement.summary: Race timing, position, energy, and results are measured under championship rules.

comparability.summary: The mechanism was declared equally available as a voting process, but popularity produced intentionally unequal assistance.

officiation.summary: Championship officials and vehicle systems administer legal deployment.

outcome_openness.summary: The race result remains open and driver-dependent, although spectators alter available resources.

consequence_structure.summary: Championship points and race results may be affected by the additional power resource.

operational_spatial_integration_profile.summary: FANBOOST is a digital spectator intervention into resource allocation, not Operational Spatial Integration. L8 participation becomes constitutive without turning spectators into performance agents.

as3_layer_notes.L1_performance_agency: Driver remains the live performer; spectators influence resources.
as3_layer_notes.L3_arena_spatial_state: Physical circuit; voting is external to arena space.
as3_layer_notes.L4_constraint_rule_execution: League rule allocates boost to selected drivers.
as3_layer_notes.L5_sensing_tracking: Votes and vehicle systems track eligibility and deployment.
as3_layer_notes.L6_measurement_comparability: Declared unequal assistance is part of the rule, not ambient equality.
as3_layer_notes.L7_officiation_outcome: Officials and car systems administer deployment.
as3_layer_notes.L9_safety_accessibility: Motorsport safety remains separate from fan voting.
as3_layer_notes.L10_governance_evidence: Mechanism and discontinuation are officially documented.

performance_agency.notes: Driver skill remains causally necessary; spectators do not drive.

constraint_integrity.notes: The intervention was an explicit championship rule.

comparability.notes: The rule intentionally creates unequal assistance based on votes.

outcome_openness.notes: Drivers still determine deployment and race execution.

evidence.source_title: FANBOOST is open — vote to influence Formula E
evidence.limitations: The mechanism was active in the Gen2 era and is now historical.
Confirms FANBOOST ended from Season 9; it does not quantify competitive effect.

objections: Popularity-based assistance raises fairness questions even when rules are transparent.
Spectator influence is not equivalent to spectator performance.
what_would_change_judgment: A format in which spectators continuously execute skill-dependent actions that directly control the competitive object.

provisional_finding.summary: Spectator influence can become constitutive to resource allocation without becoming Performance Agency, officiation, or Spatiality. The ontology needs a participatory rule/resource actor relation.

limitations: FANBOOST is discontinued and analyzed as a historical rule mechanism.
